study.question: Does the small conditional click-AUC utility of aligned auxiliary-mask membership depend on feedback rows contributing gradients through the primary scorer Dice population, beyond their forward values, count weights and preserved auxiliary learning?
study.hypothesis: Observed native full-minus-counts AUC is +0.0000604313908928; balanced weighting changes this to -0.0000883775736712. The prior permutation control is close to counts-only, and blind replacement is worse. These fixed-seed outcomes do not establish useful semantic event assignment. Source inspection shows the click head reads uniform rows, while membership feedback rows enter the shared Dice normalization population and auxiliary feedback heads. Detaching feedback-row inputs immediately before each primary Dice may remove the small aligned-content advantage if its utility depends on this backward coupling. Full-versus-counts crossed with attached-versus-blocked inputs separates this pathway from forward membership content at a common state. Masks are derived from historical action tokens in the pinned loader, so the question is architectural utility, not incremental Shannon information.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary text lines 260-335 describes unnormalized target-conditioned activation and Dice batch/running statistics. Inherit those operators; probe which compressed feedback-row cotangents affect their optimization. This is a local attribution study, not a DIN reproduction or priority claim.

Pinned Dice uses BatchNorm1d affine=False, eps=1e-9, momentum=0.01 plus learned alpha. Retain native forward, state updates and derivative for retained inputs; detach rows 1,2 before each primary Dice only.

Pinned benchmark forward lines 123-170 initializes separate task hubs using task masks then aggregates/broadcasts. This study retains the incumbent union-stratum compressed scorer and tests a normalization backward path. Original INFNet paper is provenance-only and not fully available; equivalence and novelty remain unverified.
Pinned lines 383-408 and 524-577 build masks deterministically from historical action strings/IDs, mask padding and set target action to zero. No loader or visibility changes are made.

study.proposed_difference: Two parameter-free controls detach only rows 1 and 2 of each seven-row primary Dice input during training, after expansion of folded representatives and before EACH Dice. Row 0 and support rows 3..6 retain ordinary gradients. Values, occupancy, count weights, batch/running-statistic updates and native Dice alpha are unchanged at a common state. The auxiliary functional scorer and all task losses are untouched. Both detached and attached paths are surrogate training operators because the inherited context VJP already is one. The unmodified full and counts sources are submitted byte-identically as utility controls.
predictions: At identical state and inputs, attached and blocked pairs have equal four-task forward values and native buffer updates; evaluation is identical and no labels are read in forward.

If feedback normalization backward coupling explains the native full/counts gap, blocking reduces that gap: the predeclared difference-of-differences interaction is positive. No effect-size threshold or statistical significance is inferred from this single seed.

Parameters remain 32192421 and scorer row/affine counts remain fixed. The new gate adds arange/where work and may reduce some backward cost; host timings determine net cost. No efficiency improvement is assumed.
falsifiers: Any forward/buffer mismatch at a shared state, altered module initialization, invalid-history dependence, nonfinite backward or changed loss/auxiliary ownership invalidates attribution and must stop scoring until corrected.
A stable full-minus-counts gap after blocking undermines this backward-path explanation; prioritize forward population or auxiliary mediation controls instead.
A zero or negative native content gap on a later host-authorized paired seed undermines robust conditional aligned-assignment utility; repeating the same deterministic seed is not repetition.
A gain fully explained by measured extra cost or any capacity mismatch is not evidence for justified conditional membership utility.
alternative_explanations: A modified backward operator changes subsequent optimization and running moments; fixed-state forward equality does not imply equal trained predictions.
Feedback content also affects auxiliary heads/context transfer, which remain present in both gate states; residual utility is not automatically a forward-normalization mechanism.
Counts-only preserves union counts, not per-task identity; the inherited model uses the union of cart/fav/buy.
One frozen seed and adaptive validation history give provisional evidence, not significance or independent repetition.
Native count weighting interacts with content; the preceding balanced factorial already reverses the content contrast.
A generic effect of gradient truncation may improve quality in both full and counts arms without supporting aligned membership.
Padding rows remain inherited zero-valued normalization slots. This experiment does not establish production point-in-time validity of released feedback.
